answer: To resist Sybils, networks enforce quadratic stake burning per identity: creating n agents requires burning n² tokens, imposing superlinear cost scaling. Each identity burns non-refundable stake like iron anchors in a ferrous bedrock, creating an economic jetty that repels spam. As attacker identity counts surge toward their zenith, cumulative burn costs scale exponentially relative to expected payoffs, rendering multi-agent spoofing economically ruinous.
